subject: Whether the four ie sources carrying automation_allowed:false still need it
method: scripts/check_robots.py against the URL a round would actually visit, query string included; entry page opened once in a browser to see what it presents.
outcome: Three confirmed refused by the site's own published rules and left as they were. One (jobs-ie) carried a constraint the site does not assert, and is enabled.

results.note: Whole host refused. Also needs a signed-in account, so any automation would run under the user's own credentials against terms that forbid it.
The search listing is allowed (allow: /) but the job detail page is refused, and the detail page is where the JD is. Operator terms separately forbid agentic access.
The landing page is allowed and the search with a query string is not, which is what the recorded constraint already said. The two human paths stay.

entry_page_observed.consent_dialog: standard, with an explicit Just Necessary button

results.decision: automation_allowed true, public_read_only_page added, constraint removed
results.note: robots.txt asserts nothing about these paths and the site presents no access control. The same market's other local_job_board, irishjobs-ie, was already automation_allowed:true on the same footing; the two were inconsistent with no evidence behind the difference.

not_examined: jobs-ac-uk carries the same respect_site_access_controls constraint and was not re-checked here. It is a uk source and nobody looked at it; the flag stays until someone does.
